subject: Next steps — dedicated capacity deep-dive & throughput sizing
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwave.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing and next steps

Connor / Marissa —

Thanks again for a helpful discovery call earlier today. To move toward a Dedicated capacity conversation and sizing deep-dive, our engineering leaders asked me to share a quick summary of what we expect on day one and the primary questions we want to answer during the sizing session. Hope this helps you pick the right attendees.

Quick context (high level):
- Primary workload: document-processing + chat summarization for enterprise customers.
- Peak traffic profile (approx): 600 concurrent users during peak windows, ~12 requests/sec sustained, spikes to ~40 requests/sec for short bursts.
- Average prompt length: 350 tokens; expected response length: 150–200 tokens.

What we want to prove in the sizing call:
1) Throughput targets for a single dedicated pool to handle sustained 12 r/s with burst headroom to 40 r/s.
2) End-to-end P95 latency targets under realistic batching and caching assumptions.
3) Token cost estimates and recommended quantization profile for our workload.
4) Network egress and VPC peering considerations for on-prem connections.

I've attached a small sample file (finwave_current_qps.csv) with our 48-hour sample profile and a few annotated latency outliers. Please let us know what additional telemetry you need beforehand.

Availability: can you propose 2 windows for a 60–75 minute technical deep-dive (one for next week and one for the week after)? We are US-PST based; our SRE, backend lead (Oliver), and security lead will attend.

Best,
Priya Shah
Product Operations Lead
FinWave

Attachments: finwave_current_qps.csv (csv)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 16:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and next steps

Priya —

Thanks for the clear summary and for sending the sample QPS. This is exactly the level of detail that helps us size quickly. Proposed next steps and slots:

Proposed slots (60–75 min deep-dive, PST):
- Option A: Thu 2026-12-10 10:00–11:15 PST
- Option B: Tue 2026-12-14 09:00–10:15 PST

Suggested attendees from Redwood:
- Connor O'Brien (Solutions) — will lead the throughput/l4 planning
- Marissa Cole (Sales Eng) — will coordinate runbook and account logistics
- Ben Carter (SWE, Inference) — will join for kernel/quantization discussion

Agenda (draft):
1) 10m — goal alignment & success criteria
2) 20m — FinWave load profile walkthrough (you / Oliver)
3) 25m — Redwood sizing exercise (throughput / pool sizing / burst handling)
4) 15m — networking, encryption, data retention notes
5) 5–15m — open items & next steps

Prep from our side: I attached a redwood_capacity_prep_checklist.pdf with items we typically ask for before a sizing call — if you can drop any missing telemetry into that checklist it speeds the first pass.

If either slot works, let me know which one you prefer and we’ll lock it (and I’ll send a calendar invite). If you need different times, happy to propose additional windows.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_capacity_prep_checklist.pdf
From: Oliver West <oliver.west@finwave.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and next steps

Connor / Priya —

Thanks — Option A (Thu 12/10 at 10am PST) works for our team. A couple quick asks so the deep-dive is most effective:

- We'll share a short latency sample file before the call (attached) showing 99th-percentile spikes when we load test.
- Can you confirm whether you prefer us to send raw request logs or aggregated histograms? Which helps Redwood sizing better?
- For encryption/retention: we need to confirm token retention limits and KMS integration options — can that be covered in the 15m networking/security block?

Thanks — Oliver
VP, Backend Engineering
FinWave

Attachments: finwave_latency_samples.txt
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver West <oliver.west@finwave.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finwave.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 11:37:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing and next steps

Oliver / Priya —

Great — locking Option A for now and we'll send a calendar invite shortly. Answering your questions:

- Raw logs are helpful but aggregated histograms (1s/10s buckets) with a sample of raw traces for anomalies is our usual sweet spot. Either works — if you prefer one format we can adapt.
- Security block: yes, we'll include a short KMS/integration overview and token retention controls; our security architect will join for that section.

Internal note: Ben — please plan to bring two sample quantization profiles and an initial cost estimate matrix for the workload Oliver shared. Connor — can you draft the sizing worksheet and share it 24h before the call?

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook-template.docx (internal prep)
